exam_points: Three approaches: isolation, direct detection, indirect (serology).
Right specimen, right time; transport at 4 °C, do not freeze enveloped viruses.
Cell culture with cytopathic effect: historical gold standard.
Antigen tests: fast, no live virus needed (EIA, IF, rapid tests).
HBsAg and HIV p24 are antigens detected by ELISA.
PCR: denaturation, annealing, extension; RT step for RNA viruses.
Real-time PCR: Ct inversely proportional to viral load.
Sequencing detects resistance and genotypes.
IgM = recent infection; IgG = past infection or immunity; rising IgG = recent.

deeper.title: Why a negative rapid antigen test does not rule out infection
deeper.html: Rapid antigen tests need a lot of viral protein in the sample. Early in infection, late in recovery, or with a poor swab, the amount may be below their detection limit while PCR, which amplifies a few copies millions of times, is still positive. That is why a negative rapid test in a symptomatic patient is often repeated or confirmed by PCR, while a positive rapid test is usually trusted.

exam_points: Main viruses: rotavirus, norovirus, sapovirus, adenovirus 40/41, astrovirus.
Transmission faeco-oral: hands, food, water, surfaces.
Rotavirus: Reoviridae, dsRNA, 11 segments; children < 5; winter.
VP7 (G) and VP4 (P) carry neutralising epitopes.
Norovirus: Caliciviridae, (+)ssRNA; outbreaks at all ages; hospital diarrhoea.
Naked viruses resist alcohol rubs: use soap and water, bleach.
Treatment: rehydration; no antiviral.
Rotavirus oral vaccine > 90% effective against severe disease; no norovirus vaccine yet.

deeper.title: Why cruise ships and hospitals get norovirus outbreaks
deeper.html: Norovirus is ideal for closed settings: fewer than 100 particles can infect, vomiting sprays particles into the air and onto surfaces, the naked capsid survives for days and resists alcohol gels, and immunity after infection is short and strain-specific. Controlling an outbreak therefore means isolating the sick, cleaning with chlorine, washing hands with soap and water, and keeping staff off work for 48 hours after symptoms stop.

exam_points: A and E: faeco-oral, acute; B, C, D: blood-borne, can be chronic.
HAV: picornavirus, anti-HAV IgM = acute, never chronic, vaccine.
HEV: waterborne; dangerous in pregnancy; chronic in immunocompromised.
HBV: DNA virus with reverse transcription; blood, sex, mother-to-child.
HBV chronicity: ~5% in adults, 80-95% in infants.
HBsAg > 6 months = chronic; anti-HBs = recovery/vaccine; anti-HBc IgM = acute.
HBeAg = active replication; anti-HBe = low replication.
HDV needs HBsAg; superinfection → severe chronic disease.
HCV: Flaviviridae, 7 genotypes, mostly chronic, no vaccine.
HCV: antibody screen, then RNA; DAAs cure > 95%.

deeper.title: Why every newborn gets hepatitis B vaccine
deeper.html: A baby infected at birth has a 80-95% chance of lifelong infection, because the immature immune system tolerates the virus. Decades later, many of these children develop cirrhosis or liver cancer. Giving the first dose of vaccine within 24 hours of birth, plus immunoglobulin when the mother is HBsAg-positive, blocks most mother-to-child transmission. That is why HBV vaccine sits in the infant hexavalent schedule and why pregnant women are screened.

exam_points: Herpesviruses: large enveloped dsDNA viruses; nuclear replication.
All establish lifelong latency with reactivation.
Latent DNA is episomal, not integrated; no replication → escapes drugs.
α (HSV, VZV): sensory ganglia; β (CMV): glands, blood; γ (EBV): lymphocytes.
HSV-1: oral, eye, brain. HSV-2: genital, neonatal.
HSV encephalitis: temporal, necrotising; emergency (aciclovir).
VZV: chickenpox, then shingles in a dermatome.
EBV: mononucleosis; Burkitt lymphoma, nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
Diagnosis by PCR on fresh lesions.
Aciclovir/valaciclovir; ganciclovir for CMV; varicella and shingles vaccines.

deeper.title: Why doctors start aciclovir before the test result in suspected encephalitis
deeper.html: Untreated HSV encephalitis kills most patients and leaves survivors with severe memory and behaviour problems. Aciclovir is safe, and every hour of delay worsens outcome. So a patient with fever, confusion or seizures, especially with temporal lobe signs, gets intravenous aciclovir straight away, and the CSF PCR result is used afterwards to confirm or stop it.

exam_points: HPV: naked, icosahedral, circular dsDNA, 45-55 nm.
More than 200 genotypes; cutaneous or mucosal tropism.
High-risk 16 and 18 → cervical cancer; low-risk 6 and 11 → warts.
HPV DNA in 99.7% of cervical cancers (zur Hausen, Nobel 2008).
CIN 1 → CIN 2/3 → invasive cancer over 7-30 years.
Screening: Pap smear cytology and HPV DNA test.
Vaccines are VLPs of L1 protein: 2-valent, 4-valent, 9-valent.
Koilocytes are the cytological hallmark of HPV infection.

deeper.title: How E6 and E7 turn a cell cancerous
deeper.html: High-risk HPV types make two oncoproteins. E6 marks the tumour suppressor p53 for destruction, so damaged cells no longer stop or die. E7 binds and inactivates the retinoblastoma protein (Rb), releasing the brake on the cell cycle. When the viral DNA integrates into the host genome, E6 and E7 are often over-expressed, pushing the cell towards cancer. Low-risk types 6 and 11 make weaker versions, which is why they cause warts, not cancer.

deeper.title: Why naked viruses are harder to kill
deeper.html: An envelope is a lipid membrane: detergents, alcohol, drying and bile destroy it, and without it the virus cannot attach. Naked viruses such as norovirus, rotavirus, HAV and poliovirus have only a protein capsid, which resists drying, acid, bile and alcohol hand gels. That is why they spread by the faeco-oral route, survive on surfaces, and why handwashing with soap and water is recommended during norovirus outbreaks.

exam_points: Influenza: enveloped, (−)ssRNA, 8 segments, HA and NA spikes.
Type A subtyped by HA and NA; origin in aquatic birds.
Drift (mutations) → epidemics; shift (reassortment) → pandemics.
Influenza: incubation 2-3 days, sudden fever and myalgia; pneumonia kills.
No aspirin in children (Reye's); oseltamivir within 48 h.
Flu vaccine is updated every year.
Paramyxoviruses: (−)ssRNA, non-segmented, syncytia.
Measles: Koplik spots, cephalocaudal rash; SSPE years later; MMR live vaccine.
RSV: infant bronchiolitis. Parainfluenza 1-2: croup.

deeper.title: Why the flu vaccine changes every year but measles vaccine never does
deeper.html: Measles virus is antigenically stable: its surface proteins barely change, so two doses of MMR protect for life. Influenza's haemagglutinin drifts constantly, so last year's antibodies fit this year's virus less well, and every few decades a shift brings a completely new subtype. WHO therefore chooses new vaccine strains twice a year (one for each hemisphere) from global surveillance, and people at risk need a new shot every autumn.

exam_points: Rabies: Lyssavirus, Rhabdoviridae; bullet-shaped, enveloped, (−)ssRNA.
Fatal encephalitis once symptoms start.
Dogs cause ~99% of human cases; bats in the Americas.
Incubation usually 2-3 months; shorter for bites near the head.
Early sign: pain or paraesthesia at the bite site.
Furious (hydrophobia, aerophobia) vs paralytic (~20%).
Wash the wound for 15 minutes with soap and water.
PEP: vaccine (Essen 0-3-7-14-28 or Zagreb 2-1-1) ± immunoglobulin.
Category III exposure needs vaccine + immunoglobulin.

deeper.title: Why rabies vaccine works after the bite
deeper.html: Almost every vaccine must be given before exposure. Rabies is the exception because the virus travels slowly along peripheral nerves, often for weeks, before reaching the brain. That delay gives the vaccine time to produce neutralising antibodies, and immunoglobulin injected into the wound neutralises virus locally in the meantime. Once the virus reaches the CNS and symptoms start, the window has closed, which is why PEP must never be delayed.

exam_points: Retroviruses: enveloped, 2 copies of (+)ssRNA, reverse transcriptase, integration.
HIV-1 (from chimpanzee SIV, group M pandemic); HIV-2 (sooty mangabey, West Africa, milder).
Genes: gag (p24), pol (RT, integrase, protease), env (gp120, gp41).
Entry: CD4 + CCR5 or CXCR4.
Primary infection → long asymptomatic but active phase (8-10 y) → AIDS.
AIDS: CD4 < 200/mm³, opportunistic infections and tumours.
Early diagnosis: p24 antigen and RNA; antibodies from 2-3 weeks.
Newborns of HIV+ mothers: diagnose by PCR, not antibodies.
Monitor viral load (PCR) and CD4 (flow cytometry).
HTLV-1: adult T-cell leukaemia and HAM/TSP; blood, breast milk, semen.

deeper.title: Undetectable = untransmittable
deeper.html: Large studies of couples in which one partner had HIV and took effective antiretroviral therapy found no sexual transmission when the viral load stayed undetectable. This 'U=U' message changed HIV care: treating everyone early protects the person and their partners, and is one of the pillars of HIV control alongside testing and PrEP.

exam_points: Jenner (1796) used cowpox: origin of 'vaccine'.
Vaccines induce neutralising antibodies, cytotoxic T cells and memory.
Live attenuated: MMR, varicella, yellow fever, oral polio, rotavirus; not in pregnancy or immunodeficiency.
Inactivated: rabies, injectable polio, HAV. Recombinant: HBV. VLP: HPV. mRNA/vector: SARS-CoV-2.
Passive immunisation: immediate, temporary (~4 months).
Herd immunity protects the unvaccinated.
Antivirals are hard to make selective because viruses use host machinery.
Aciclovir (1983) and AZT (1990) were landmarks; DAAs cure HCV.
Targets: entry, genome synthesis, protein processing, assembly, release.

deeper.title: How aciclovir kills only infected cells
deeper.html: Aciclovir is a prodrug. The first phosphate is added by the viral thymidine kinase of HSV or VZV, which normal cells lack, so the drug is activated almost only in infected cells. Host kinases then complete it to aciclovir triphosphate, which the viral DNA polymerase incorporates, terminating the chain. This two-step selectivity explains why aciclovir is so safe, and why HSV that loses its thymidine kinase becomes resistant (then foscarnet, which acts directly on the polymerase, is used).

figure.caption: Each step of the cycle is a target. Schematic drawn for this site.
